PullRequest.Title: Fix terminal-editor shift-drop on detached instances
PullRequest.Body:
- dispose terminal drag-and-drop observers when their instances detach from an editor container
- prevent deferred drag-and-drop initialization from attaching to a stale container
- add regression coverage for initialized and pending observers during terminal editor tab reuse

Fixes #311164

Co-authored-by: Vlad Gerasimov [vlad@vlad.studio](mailto:vlad@vlad.studio)

Scenarios.Scenario: Reuse a terminal editor container for a different terminal instance, including detaching after drag-and-drop initialization
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `TerminalEditor.setInput` synchronously detaches the old instance and attaches the new one; the new DnD controller is initialized by a zero-delay timer. The added `clear()` only synchronously disposes a fixed set of emitters/listeners and is on the tab-reuse path, but does not perform layout, I/O, or scaling work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: On a subsequent file drop, `sendPath` prepares the path and calls `TerminalProcessManager.write`, which invokes terminal process input.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: After the diff, one terminal-process input per file drop on the reused container. Before the diff, the old and new observers could each handle the same drop, producing up to two process-input calls for the demonstrated two-instance reuse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The boundary already existed for normal file drops; stale observer retention could duplicate it after container reuse. The diff reduces rather than increases this boundary cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The process input occurs only when the user drops a file, not during detach/attach. The diff removes the stale call and does not add a boundary to the editor-reuse critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One old and one new terminal per editor-input replacement. Disposal cardinality is constant: one controller store and the fixed drag listener set for the detached instance.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Initialization callbacks are queued on the UI event loop. The container-identity guard prevents a stale callback from initializing after ownership changes; the active instance still creates one observer. There is no worker pool, queue burst, or parallel boundary operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates. Cold and repeated attachment both schedule initialization; same-container `attachToElement` calls return before scheduling. Detach clears the current observer immediately.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed line disposes the MutableDisposable's prior store, whose fixed DOM listeners and controller emitters are directly visible; the test demonstrates old/new container reuse.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact frequency of terminal editor tab reuse followed by file drops is unknown, but the changed mechanism is bounded and removes work rather than adding it.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change performs constant-time cleanup on a relatively infrequent lifecycle transition and prevents duplicate event handling and process input.

Scenarios.Scenario: Detach a terminal when removing it from a panel group or moving it to the background before deferred DnD initialization runs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Group removal/backgrounding calls `detachFromElement`; the added observer clear is synchronous and fixed-size. A pending attach timer later checks the captured container against the current container and exits before allocating the controller or listeners.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One observer store per detached terminal. Across multiple terminals, cost grows linearly with the number explicitly detached, with constant work per terminal and no collection-wide scan introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All detach and deferred initialization work runs on the UI event loop. Each prior attach may have one queued timer; the new guard suppresses stale initialization rather than increasing concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or negative cache. When the terminal is later attached to a valid container, it creates a fresh observer; same-container attachments remain coalesced by the existing early return.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: direct call sites show detach during group removal/backgrounding, and MutableDisposable.clear synchronously disposes the held store.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously backgrounded terminals varies, but no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work was added, and retained DOM/listener state is reduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Cleanup bounds retained listener/controller state, while the stale-callback guard avoids eager allocation after detach.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all changed files and hunks. Traced terminal editor reuse, panel/group removal, backgrounding, deferred observer initialization, DOM listener disposal, and the file-drop process-input boundary. The PR removes stale observers and duplicate boundary work with only fixed synchronous cleanup; no actionable performance regression was introduced.
